questions.question: The highest possible oxidation states of uranium and plutonium, respectively are :
questions.explanation:
You want to transform all the LaTeX expressions to inline format with $ symbols. Here is the transformed text :

The highest possible oxidation states of uranium and plutonium can be identified by considering the electronic configurations of these elements and noting the number of valence electrons available for bonding.

Uranium (U, atomic number 92) has the electronic configuration: $ [Rn] 5f^3 6d^1 7s^2 $

Plutonium (Pu, atomic number 94) has the electronic configuration: $ [Rn] 5f^6 7s^2 $

To find the highest oxidation state, we sum the number of $d$, $f$, and $s$ electrons in the valence shell.

For uranium : $ 3 (f) + 1 (d) + 2 (s) = 6 $ So the highest oxidation state of uranium is +6.

For plutonium : $ 6 (f) + 2 (s) = 8 $ So the highest oxidation state of plutonium is +8. However, in practice, plutonium is known to exhibit a highest oxidation state of +7.

Comparing with the given options, the correct answer is :

Option D : 6 and 7.

questions.question: In chromatography, which of the following statements is incorrect for R<sub>f</sub> ?
options: R<sub>f</sub>  value depends on the type of chromatography.

Higher R<sub>f</sub>
 value means higher adsorption.

R<sub>f</sub>
 value is dependent on the mobile phase.

The value of R<sub>f</sub>
 can not be more than one.
questions.explanation:
R<sub>f</sub> = $${x \over y}$$


$$x$$ = Distance moved by the substance from baseline


$$y$$ = Distance moved by the solvent from baseline


Option A : Correct. The R<sub>f</sub> value can depend on the type of chromatography being used because different methods can use different stationary and mobile phases, which can influence how far a substance travels.



Option B : Incorrect. The R<sub>f</sub> value is actually inversely related to adsorption. A higher Rf value indicates that the substance is less strongly adsorbed to the stationary phase, and therefore moves further along with the mobile phase.



Option C : Correct. The nature of the mobile phase can greatly influence the R<sub>f</sub> value. The more compatible the substance is with the mobile phase, the further it will travel, leading to a higher Rf value.



Option D : Correct. By definition, the R<sub>f</sub> value cannot exceed one, as a substance cannot travel further than the solvent.



So, Option B is incorrect for the R<sub>f</sub> value in chromatography.

A submarine experiences a pressure of 5.05 × 10<sup>6</sup>
 Pa at a depth of d<sub>1</sub> in a sea. When it goes further to a depth
of d<sub>2</sub>, it experiences a pressure of 8.08 × 10<sup>6</sup>
 Pa. Then d<sub>2</sub> –d<sub>1</sub> is approximately (density of water = 10<sup>3</sup>
 kg/m<sup>3</sup>
and acceleration due to gravity = 10 ms<sup>–2</sup>
) :
questions.explanation:
The pressure experienced by a submarine at a certain depth in the sea is given by the formula:

$P = \rho g h$

where:

  • $P$ is the pressure
  • $\rho$ is the density of the fluid (sea water in this case)
  • $g$ is the acceleration due to gravity
  • $h$ is the height (or depth in this case)

Given:

  • $\rho = 10^3 \, kg/m^3$
  • $g = 10 \, m/s^2$

We are looking for the difference in depth, $d_2 - d_1$, which corresponds to the difference in pressure $\Delta P$:

$\Delta P = P_2 - P_1 = \rho g (d_2 - d_1)$

Rearranging the above equation, we get:

$d_2 - d_1 = \frac{\Delta P}{\rho g}$

Given:

  • $P_2 = 8.08 \times 10^6 \, Pa$
  • $P_1 = 5.05 \times 10^6 \, Pa$

$\Delta P = P_2 - P_1 = 8.08 \times 10^6 \, Pa - 5.05 \times 10^6 \, Pa = 3.03 \times 10^6 \, Pa$

So,

$d_2 - d_1 = \frac{3.03 \times 10^6 \, Pa}{10^3 \, kg/m^3 \times 10 \, m/s^2} = 303 \, m$

The closest answer among the options provided is Option C, 300 m.
